title: Greater Israel Double Tech and AI implementation network — depth 8
summary: The education-philanthropy branch has evolved into a current implementation stack spanning government policy, MAOZ collective-impact operations, school-network grants, AI human-capital planning, and named military/intelligence-background governance bridges.

data.question: How did the 5p2 education coalition evolve into the current Double Tech and national AI human-capital implementation network?
data.method: Official program and grant review, current government verification, named-person roster expansion, and deterministic set-intersection ranking.
data.framework: Separate policy adoption, operational leadership, grants, advisory participation, military or intelligence biography, and merely referenced participation.
data.scope: High-tech matriculation policy, Double Tech, MAOZ, Education Ministry implementation, school-network grants, National AI Directorate, and named people bridges.
findings: The current implementation chain is 5p2 and Top15 experience to Perlmutter Committee recommendations, government high-tech matriculation policy, measurement and grant infrastructure, and Double Tech collective-impact operations.
MAOZ reports co-leading Double Tech with the Trump Foundation and Education Ministry, with approximately 260 launch participants and 22 working tables.
The foundation has active implementation grants for principal training and multi-year school-network expansion through at least 2029.
The National AI Directorate's July 2026 plan includes school AI literacy, university programs, workforce training, industry consultation, and national security framing.

Yair Schindel and Liat Nadai Arad create independently documented MAOZ governance bridges into Digital Israel, venture capital, special forces, Military Intelligence cyber command, hospital AI, and private technology boards.
MAOZ launch communications referenced the National AI Directorate and Erez Askal, but the reviewed evidence does not establish a formal Directorate governance role in Double Tech.
conclusions: The network is now an active state-philanthropy-nonprofit implementation architecture rather than only an education advocacy coalition.
Military and intelligence biographies are present in governance and adjacent policy layers, but do not by themselves establish military command over the education program.
recommendations: Retrieve the Double Tech steering committee roster, terms of reference, funding ledger, work-table outputs, onboarding records, and partner commitments.
Resolve which Education Ministry implementation plan and budget were formally approved and identify procurement and grant vehicles.
Map the AI Directorate's formal role, if any, in school human-capital programs and distinguish attendance or public endorsement from governance.
Track school-network disbursements and outcome measurements through 2029.
Resolve MAOZ funders, board conflicts, government joint-venture agreements, and implementing contractors.
counterarguments: Cross-sector implementation may reflect ordinary expertise and capacity building rather than capture or coordinated political control.
Military or intelligence backgrounds may be incidental to later civilian governance roles.
limitations: Double Tech governance documents and funding records were not publicly located.
Some launch-participant claims rely on official organization social-media posts rather than formal minutes.
The exact government budget and approval status has shifted across foundation pages and requires primary decision documents.
unresolved: Double Tech steering committee and legal vehicle.
Education Ministry budget, procurement, and implementation approval.
Formal National AI Directorate role in Double Tech.
Outcome data and disbursements for current grants.
